title: Ninth Word First Point The Meaning Of Prayer

questions.question: What three things are prayers said to give to Allah?
questions.answer: Glory, greatness, and thanks.

questions.question: How can a person show glory to Allah in prayer?
questions.answer: With words and with actions.

questions.question: What does a person say to honor Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: Allah is the Greatest.

questions.question: What does “All praise belongs to Allah” show?
questions.answer: Thankfulness to Allah.

questions.question: Which parts of a person are named in giving praise?
questions.answer: The heart, the tongue, and the body.

questions.question: What picture is used for glorifying, honoring Allah’s greatness, and praising Him?
questions.answer: They are like seeds of prayer.

questions.question: If they are like seeds, what does that help us understand about prayer?
questions.answer: They are basic parts that help prayer grow.

questions.question: Where in the prayer are these three meanings found?
questions.answer: In all the words and actions.

questions.question: Why are these blessed phrases said thirty-three times after the prayer?
questions.answer: To make the meaning stronger and repeat it well.

questions.question: What do those short phrases do for the prayer’s meaning?
questions.answer: They confirm and summarize it.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage about prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer means honoring Allah, praising Him, and thanking Him.

questions.question: Who is praised and thanked in the prayer?
questions.answer: Almighty Allah.

questions.question: When a person speaks and acts with respect for Allah’s highness, what is he doing?
questions.answer: He is worshipping and honoring Allah.

questions.question: When a person says that Allah is greater than all, what is he doing?
questions.answer: He is lifting up Allah’s perfection and greatness.

questions.question: Why is thankfulness joined with beauty in the passage?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s perfect beauty deserves thanks.

questions.question: Are prayer words only about speaking, or also about doing?
questions.answer: They are about both speaking and doing.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the heart in prayer?
questions.answer: The heart also praises and thanks Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare these three meanings to seeds?
questions.answer: Because they are the starting parts of prayer.

questions.question: What can we infer if these meanings are in every part of prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer is full of remembering Allah in many ways.

questions.question: After prayer, why are the special words repeated many times instead of only once?
questions.answer: So the message stays strong and clear.

questions.question: What are the three key meanings inside the prayers?
questions.answer: Glorifying Allah, honoring His greatness, and thanking Him.

questions.question: What does glorifying Allah tell us about Him?
questions.answer: He is above all weakness and is most high.

questions.question: What does honoring Allah’s greatness tell us about Him?
questions.answer: He is perfect and greater than everything.

questions.question: What does praising Allah with thanks tell us about Him?
questions.answer: He is full of beauty and goodness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about using the body in prayer?
questions.answer: The body also helps worship Allah.

questions.question: Which is more complete in the passage: praising with only the tongue or with heart, tongue, and body?
questions.answer: With heart, tongue, and body.

questions.question: What does it mean that these three are in all the prayer’s actions and words?
questions.answer: Every part of prayer carries these meanings.

questions.question: What happens after the prayer to support these meanings?
questions.answer: The blessed words are repeated thirty-three times.

questions.question: What is the purpose of repeating them thirty-three times?
questions.answer: To strengthen the prayer’s meaning.

questions.question: How does the passage describe those repeated words at the end?
questions.answer: As short summaries that confirm the meaning.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is prayer really about?
questions.answer: It is about worshipping Allah with honor, praise, and thanks.

questions.question: What two ways are named for showing honor to Allah’s glory?
questions.answer: By speech and by actions.

questions.question: If someone says Allah is the Greatest, which idea of Allah is being lifted up?
questions.answer: His perfect greatness.

questions.question: If someone thanks Allah from the heart, what part of prayer is that showing?
questions.answer: Praise and gratitude.

questions.question: Why is it important that the body is mentioned with the heart and tongue?
questions.answer: Because prayer is done with the whole person.

questions.question: What does the seed example teach about the three meanings?
questions.answer: They are the beginning and core of prayer.

questions.question: Does the passage limit these meanings to one part of prayer?
questions.answer: No, they are in every part.

questions.question: What number is given for repeating the blessed words after prayer?
questions.answer: Thirty-three.

questions.question: Why are these repeated phrases called concise summaries?
questions.answer: Because they are short words that gather the prayer’s big meanings.

questions.question: Name one thing prayer gives to Allah besides thanks.
questions.answer: Glory or greatness.

questions.question: What does a Muslim do before Allah’s high majesty according to the passage?
questions.answer: He honors and worships Allah.

questions.question: What is being shown when a person says Allah is greater than all perfection we know?
questions.answer: Allah’s perfect greatness is being honored.

questions.question: What three parts of a person join in thanking Allah?
questions.answer: The heart, the tongue, and the body.

questions.question: Why does the passage join words and actions together more than once?
questions.answer: Because prayer is said and done.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the three meanings and the prayer as a whole?
questions.answer: The prayer is built from them.

questions.question: How do we know these meanings are very important in prayer?
questions.answer: They appear in every part and are repeated after prayer.

questions.question: What is one reason for repeating the blessed words many times after prayer?
questions.answer: To make the meanings stronger in the person.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Prayer is full of honoring, magnifying, and thanking Allah.

questions.question: What three big ideas are at the center of prayer in this passage?
questions.answer: Glorifying Allah, saying He is the Greatest, and praising Him with thanks.

questions.question: When someone glorifies Allah, what is he doing with his words and actions?
questions.answer: He is showing deep respect and worship.

questions.question: What does saying Allah is the Greatest help a person remember about Allah?
questions.answer: That Allah is perfectly great.

questions.question: What does praising Allah with thanks help a person remember about Allah?
questions.answer: That Allah is full of beauty and blessings.

questions.question: Does the passage show prayer as only talking, only moving, or both?
questions.answer: Both.

questions.question: What comparison is used to explain the three meanings in prayer?
questions.answer: They are compared to seeds.

questions.question: What repeated practice after prayer helps keep these meanings strong?
questions.answer: Saying the blessed phrases thirty-three times each.

questions.question: What do those short repeated phrases do for someone who prays?
questions.answer: They remind him again of prayer’s meaning.
